# Extra Medium — full text for AI readers

Extra Medium (legal name Extra Medium LLC) is a founder-led strategy, creative, growth and technology studio and product lab headquartered in Virginia Beach, Virginia, USA, with presence in Chicago and London and clients across the US and UK. Tagline: "Whatever the medium. Make it matter." Positioning line: "Your business doesn't need more marketing. It needs something worth noticing."

Senior people only, and the engagement shape and price in writing before work begins.

## What Extra Medium does

The studio practices six chapters under one senior team:

1. Launch — positioning, naming, brand identity, website, go-to-market and product launch for things that do not exist yet or have not been introduced properly.
2. Reinvent — brand strategy, rebranding, messaging and website redesign for businesses that moved faster than their brand.
3. Grow — growth marketing with an owner: paid media, SEO and AI search, ecommerce and Shopify growth, lifecycle and creator channels, run as one system against revenue.
4. Lead — fractional CMO leadership for businesses that need a senior marketing brain without a permanent executive seat, plus executive and personal branding.
5. Intelligence — AI consulting, AI agents and automation wired into how a company actually operates, applied across marketing, reporting, creative development and workflow.
6. Experiences — podcasts, events and experiential marketing.

Engagement shapes: (1) fractional leadership, (2) a defined project with a clear beginning and end, scoped after the first conversation and priced with a clear range, (3) ongoing growth work. Process: a conversation, not a proposal; if the studio cannot help, it says so.

## Founder

Jeff Rimmer is Founder & Principal of Extra Medium, with more than 20 years in marketing across startups and Fortune 100 companies. Before Extra Medium he founded a digital music platform and grew it past 900,000 users. Deepest industry experience: music and entertainment, retail and ecommerce, healthcare and wellness. He leads every engagement personally. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/jeffrimmer

## Proof and range

Client work spans pre-launch startups, founder-led growth brands, makers and manufacturers, and Fortune 500 retail — including a growth system for a high-growth nutritional supplement brand, global marketing and post-acquisition brand integration for a radiation-protection manufacturer, ecommerce and app optimization for a Fortune 500 retailer's three banners, an enterprise licensing launch for a music company (early adopters included Microsoft and Baylor University), and the B2B positioning and website for a contract manufacturer's brand-creation division.

## Extra Medium Labs and Magpie

Extra Medium Labs is the studio's product lab, where it builds and operates its own products. The flagship product is Magpie (https://magpielocal.com), a local creator marketing platform:

- Problem: influencer marketing skipped local; neighborhood businesses need the local creators their customers actually follow.
- How it works: a business makes an offer (a comped visit or a paid booking); a local creator visits; the creator posts honestly (one post or reel plus two stories within 48 hours, disclosed); the business sees tracked results (register spend counted, media value modeled and labeled).
- Creators: free always; 500 followers is enough; tiers auto-assigned by stacked audience — Neighbors 500–2k, Locals 2k–15k, Headliners 15k+. On paid bookings creators keep 97% (business pays rate + 3%; $50 rate floor).
- Businesses: published plans on the product site; applications decided within two business days; a Visit Guarantee replaces any no-show or unposted visit.
- Status (November 2026): live platform in founding-market formation across 45 founding markets in 13 countries; home market is Virginia Beach (covering Hampton Roads), activating first. Operated by Extra Medium LLC.

Second live Labs product: Hapsta (hapsta.co), small capped live video rooms where fans hang out or play games with famous people — the celebrity sets the price, length and room size and keeps 80% of ticket revenue; waitlist open, first sessions forming. Other Labs ventures in development: Roon (family memory platform), JAWNRA (global music discovery and charts). Extra Medium also publishes Extra Extra, a magazine at https://xmedium.co/magazine/ covering marketing, advertising, music and media, including the official Magpie announcement.

## Extra Extra — the news stream (https://xmedium.co/magazine/)

Extra Extra is Extra Medium's news site: stories on marketing, advertising, music and media, plus dispatches from the lab, published continuously with the newest story first. Latest stories, newest first:

- Is SEO Dead? What AI Search Actually Changed (November 16, 2026) — https://xmedium.co/magazine/is-seo-dead/ — Short answer: No. SEO is not dead, but the job changed. People still search, only now an AI answer often comes first and cites a few clear sources. Sites that answer real questions plainly, with proof and structure machines can read, get cited. Vague, keyword-stuffed pages get skipped.
- The Chart That Lies: Popularity Tells You Who Won. Momentum Tells You Who Is Next. (November 15, 2026) — https://xmedium.co/magazine/the-chart-that-lies/ — Short answer: a popularity chart ranks what already won, adding up total plays after the fact; momentum measures how fast a song or artist is rising right now, the only version of the number you can still act on. JAWNRA, in development at Extra Medium Labs, is a music discovery and chart platform built to measure momentum instead of totals.

- How Much Does a Marketing Agency Cost? — https://xmedium.co/how-much-does-a-marketing-agency-cost/ — Short answer: A marketing agency typically charges a monthly retainer, and the honest answer is that the range is wide because the work is: a narrow, well-defined scope costs far less than a full growth function. What you are really buying is seniority, scope and speed &mdash; and the cheapest quote is usually the most expensive mistake.
- Why Is My Marketing Not Working? — https://xmedium.co/why-is-my-marketing-not-working/ — Short answer: Marketing usually fails for one of five reasons: there is no strategy underneath it, it is aimed at the wrong audience, the offer is weak, the follow-through stops early, or success is being measured in likes instead of revenue. The fix starts with diagnosis, not more activity &mdash; more of the wrong thing is just more.
- Marketing Agency vs. Freelancer — https://xmedium.co/marketing-agency-vs-freelancer/ — Short answer: A freelancer is the right call when the job is one skill, well defined, and someone inside your business can direct it. An agency is the right call when you need several skills working from one strategy. The trap is hiring freelance hands when the thing you actually lack is direction.
- How to Choose a Marketing Agency — https://xmedium.co/how-to-choose-a-marketing-agency/ — Short answer: Choose an agency the way you would hire a senior employee: ask who will actually do the work, how they decide what to do, and how they will report against revenue. Beware case-study theater &mdash; polished results from other people&rsquo;s budgets. A good agency can explain its first 90 days on your business before you sign anything.
- Small Business Marketing Mistakes — https://xmedium.co/small-business-marketing-mistakes/ — Short answer: The same five, on repeat: boosting posts instead of running a strategy, copying what big brands do, leading with no real offer, never following up on the interest marketing creates, and only marketing when sales dip. None of them is a budget problem. All of them are fixable in the order they are listed.
- How Local Businesses Get More Customers — https://xmedium.co/how-local-businesses-get-more-customers/ — Short answer: Local businesses win customers by being findable at the exact moment someone nearby is ready to buy: a complete Google Business Profile, strong local search presence, a steady flow of real reviews, and a visible life in the neighborhood &mdash; local creators, community presence, and offers a person can act on today, not someday.
- Are Paid Ads Worth It for a Small Business? — https://xmedium.co/are-paid-ads-worth-it-for-small-business/ — Short answer: Paid ads are worth it when three things are true: the margin on a new customer covers the cost of buying one, people are already searching for what you sell, and someone follows up fast when interest arrives. Miss any one of the three and ads do not fail loudly &mdash; they just quietly burn the budget.
- Influencer Marketing for Local Businesses — https://xmedium.co/influencer-marketing-for-local-businesses/ — Short answer: Yes, when the influencer is actually local. A creator whose followers live in your trade area can fill tables, book appointments and move product in a way a celebrity post never will, because their audience can act on it today. The discipline is checking local reach before you book &mdash; not follower count, which measures the wrong map.
